## Choosing a geom

A **geom** is a layer's drawing method: points, lines, bars, text, or another mark.
Some geoms also compute a default summary before drawing.

| Your data/question | Start with |
|---|---|
| Two numeric measurements per person | `geom_point()` |
| One numeric variable's distribution | `geom_histogram()` |
| A numeric outcome across groups | `geom_boxplot()` plus points |
| Counts of records by category | `geom_bar()` |
| Heights already calculated in a table | `geom_col()` |
| Repeated measurements within a person | `geom_line()` with `group = id` |

## Optional: complete ggplot2 geom catalogue {#geom-catalogue}

The next slides list the exported `geom_*()` functions in the ggplot2 version
used to render this deck, including aliases and older interfaces.

- They are a **lookup reference**, not a memorization requirement.
- Extension-package geoms, such as `ggrepel::geom_text_repel()`, are separate.
- `stat_*()`, scales, and themes are different function families.

[Skip the catalogue and continue to distributions](#core-distributions)

[Official ggplot2 function reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/index.html)

```{r}
#| label: geom-catalogue-data
#| include: false
geom_catalogue <- list(
  points = c(
    geom_point = "One mark at each x/y location",
    geom_jitter = "Points with position offsets to reveal overlap",
    geom_count = "Point area represents the number at an x/y location",
    geom_rug = "Small marks along the plot margins",
    geom_text = "Text from a label variable",
    geom_label = "Text with a background box"),
  paths = c(
    geom_line = "Connect observations in x order within each group",
    geom_path = "Connect observations in their row order",
    geom_step = "Connect observations using steps",
    geom_segment = "Separate segments, with start and end coordinates",
    geom_curve = "Curved connections between endpoints",
    geom_spoke = "Segments specified by angle and length"),
  distributions = c(
    geom_histogram = "Counts or densities in numeric bins",
    geom_freqpoly = "A line through binned frequencies",
    geom_density = "A smooth estimate of a one-variable density",
    geom_dotplot = "Stacked dots in bins",
    geom_boxplot = "Median, quartiles, whiskers, and extreme points",
    geom_violin = "A mirrored density for each group",
    geom_qq = "Sample quantiles against reference quantiles",
    geom_qq_line = "A reference line for a Q-Q display"),
  bars = c(
    geom_bar = "Count records by category by default",
    geom_col = "Draw supplied y values as bar heights",
    geom_area = "Filled region to a baseline, stacked by default",
    geom_ribbon = "Region between supplied ymin and ymax",
    geom_rect = "Rectangles defined by boundary coordinates",
    geom_tile = "Rectangles defined by centres and dimensions",
    geom_raster = "Efficient equal-sized rectangular cells"),
  intervals = c(
    geom_pointrange = "Point estimate and interval",
    geom_linerange = "Interval alone",
    geom_errorbar = "Interval with end caps",
    geom_crossbar = "Central value across an interval box",
    geom_errorbarh = "Older horizontal error-bar interface (deprecated)"),
  fits = c(
    geom_smooth = "Fitted trend with an optional uncertainty band",
    geom_quantile = "Conditional quantile regression lines",
    geom_function = "Evaluate and draw a supplied function",
    geom_abline = "Lines specified by intercept and slope",
    geom_hline = "Horizontal reference lines",
    geom_vline = "Vertical reference lines",
    geom_blank = "Invisible layer, useful for establishing scale ranges"),
  surfaces = c(
    geom_bin_2d = "Counts in rectangular x/y bins",
    geom_hex = "Counts in hexagonal x/y bins",
    geom_density_2d = "Contours of an estimated x/y density",
    geom_density_2d_filled = "Filled regions of an estimated x/y density",
    geom_contour = "Contour lines for supplied grid values z",
    geom_contour_filled = "Filled contour regions for supplied grid values z"),
  maps = c(
    geom_polygon = "Closed shapes from ordered vertices",
    geom_map = "Values joined to a separate map polygon table",
    geom_sf = "Geometry from an sf spatial object",
    geom_sf_text = "Text located using sf geometry",
    geom_sf_label = "Boxed text located using sf geometry"),
  aliases = c(
    geom_bin2d = "Alias of geom_bin_2d",
    geom_density2d = "Alias of geom_density_2d",
    geom_density2d_filled = "Alias of geom_density_2d_filled")
)
exported_geoms <- sort(getNamespaceExports("ggplot2"))
exported_geoms <- exported_geoms[startsWith(exported_geoms, "geom_")]
listed_geoms <- unlist(lapply(geom_catalogue, names), use.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(listed_geoms), setequal(exported_geoms, listed_geoms))
show_geoms <- function(group) {
  entries <- geom_catalogue[[group]]
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Function = paste0("`", names(entries), "()`"),
    Purpose = unname(entries)
  ), row.names = FALSE)
}
gallery_pair <- function(left, right) {
  grid::grid.newpage()
  print(left + theme_minimal(base_size = 15),
        vp = grid::viewport(x = 0.25, width = 0.48))
  print(right + theme_minimal(base_size = 15),
        vp = grid::viewport(x = 0.75, width = 0.48))
}
gallery_summary <- trial |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(m = mean(sbp_12), se = sd(sbp_12) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop")
gallery_time <- trial_long |>
  group_by(arm, week) |>
  summarise(m = mean(sbp), se = sd(sbp) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
```

## Geom reference: points and labels {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("points")
```

## Geom examples: points and jitter {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-points
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
gallery_pair(
  ggplot(trial, aes(sbp_0, sbp_12, colour = arm)) +
    geom_point() + scale_colour_manual(values = arm_col, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "geom_point()", x = "Baseline SBP", y = "Week 12 SBP"),
  ggplot(trial, aes(arm, sbp_12, colour = arm)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = arm_col, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "geom_jitter()", x = NULL, y = "Week 12 SBP")
)
```

Points show a relationship between two measurements. Jitter separates
overlapping observations within categories. Both show individual participants.

## Geom reference: connected observations {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("paths")
```

Connecting observations implies a relationship or order. It is usually
inappropriate to connect unrelated participants just because their rows are adjacent.

## Geom examples: line and step {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-lines
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
gallery_pair(
  ggplot(gallery_time, aes(week, m, colour = arm)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = arm_col, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 6, 12)) +
    labs(title = "geom_line()", x = "Week", y = "Mean SBP"),
  ggplot(data.frame(day = c(0, 2, 5, 8), dose = c(0, 10, 20, 10)),
         aes(day, dose)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 1, colour = "#0072B2") +
    labs(title = "geom_step()", x = "Day", y = "Dose (mg)")
)
```

A line connects measured summaries. A step can represent a dose held constant
until the next change. The right-hand schedule is a separate synthetic example.

## Geom reference: distributions {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("distributions")
```

## Geom examples: distribution summaries {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-distributions
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
gallery_pair(
  ggplot(trial, aes(sbp_0)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 8, fill = "#0072B2", colour = "white") +
    labs(title = "geom_histogram()", x = "Baseline SBP", y = "Count"),
  ggplot(trial, aes(arm, sbp_12, fill = arm)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.4) + geom_boxplot(width = 0.15) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = arm_col, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "geom_violin() + geom_boxplot()", x = NULL, y = "Week 12 SBP")
)
```

The histogram groups observations into numeric bins. A violin describes a
smoothed distribution, while the overlaid box marks its quartiles and median.

## Geom examples: bars and a ribbon {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-bars-ribbon
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
gallery_pair(
  ggplot(trial, aes(site_f)) + geom_bar(fill = "#0072B2") +
    labs(title = "geom_bar()", x = NULL, y = "Participants"),
  ggplot(subset(gallery_time, arm == "Treatment"), aes(week, m)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se),
                fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 6, 12)) +
    labs(title = "geom_ribbon() + geom_line()", x = "Week", y = "Mean SBP")
)
```

Bars show counts. The ribbon fills a supplied lower-to-upper range, here
approximate 95% intervals for the treatment-arm mean at each visit.

## Geom reference: intervals {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("intervals")
```

For new horizontal error bars, use `geom_errorbar(orientation = "y")`
with `xmin` and `xmax`. The plotting function does not determine whether your
interval means SD, SE, or a confidence interval.

## Geom examples: two ways to draw an interval {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-intervals
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
interval_plot <- ggplot(gallery_summary,
  aes(arm, m, ymin = m - 1.96 * se, ymax = m + 1.96 * se)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean week 12 SBP")
gallery_pair(
  interval_plot + geom_pointrange(colour = "#0072B2") +
    labs(title = "geom_pointrange()"),
  interval_plot + geom_errorbar(width = 0.15, colour = "#0072B2") +
    geom_point(size = 2, colour = "#0072B2") +
    labs(title = "geom_errorbar() + geom_point()")
)
```

These show the same means and approximate 95% confidence intervals.
Pointrange draws both marks; errorbar supplies the interval with end caps.

## Geom reference: fits and reference lines {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("fits")
```

## Geom examples: fitted and reference lines {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-fits
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
relationship <- ggplot(trial, aes(sbp_0, sbp_12)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55) + labs(x = "Baseline SBP", y = "Week 12 SBP")
gallery_pair(
  relationship + geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "#0072B2") +
    labs(title = 'geom_smooth(method = "lm")'),
  relationship + geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1,
                              linetype = 2, colour = "#D55E00") +
    labs(title = "geom_abline()")
)
```

The fitted line summarizes a relationship in the data. The identity line
marks equality between visits and needs no fitted model.

## Geom reference: two-dimensional patterns {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("surfaces")
```

`geom_hex()` needs the **hexbin** package. Counts, estimated densities, and
supplied surface values answer different questions.

## Geom examples: binned counts and contours {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-surfaces
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
surface_grid <- expand.grid(x = seq_len(nrow(volcano)),
                            y = seq_len(ncol(volcano)))
surface_grid$z <- as.vector(volcano)
gallery_pair(
  ggplot(trial, aes(sbp_0, sbp_12)) +
    geom_bin_2d(bins = 8) + scale_fill_viridis_c() +
    labs(title = "geom_bin_2d()", x = "Baseline SBP", y = "Week 12 SBP",
         fill = "Count"),
  ggplot(surface_grid, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
    geom_contour(colour = "#0072B2") + coord_equal() +
    labs(title = "geom_contour()", x = "Grid column", y = "Grid row")
)
```

Left: counts of participants in x/y bins. Right: equal-value lines from R's
built-in `volcano` elevation grid. Contours require surface values, not just x/y pairs.

## Geom reference: maps and shapes {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("maps")
```

The `geom_sf*()` functions use the **sf** package and spatial data structures.
Spatial analysis is outside this session's core material.

## Geom example: regions defined by vertices {.gallery}

```{r}
#| label: gallery-polygons
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.4
regions <- data.frame(
  region = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),
  x = c(0, 2, 2, 0, 2, 4, 4, 2), y = c(0, 0, 2, 3, 0, 1, 3, 2)
)
ggplot(regions, aes(x, y, group = region, fill = region)) +
  geom_polygon(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_equal() + scale_fill_manual(values = c(A = "#0072B2", B = "#E69F00")) +
  labs(title = "geom_polygon(): two synthetic regions", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_void(base_size = 17)
```

Each group supplies one shape's vertices in boundary order. Real geographic
work commonly uses `geom_sf()` with spatial geometry instead of hand-entered vertices.

## Geom reference: aliases and package version {.geom-reference}

```{r}
#| echo: false
show_geoms("aliases")
```

This deck lists **`r length(exported_geoms)` exported names**, including aliases,
for **ggplot2 `r as.character(packageVersion("ggplot2"))`**.

Use `?geom_point` or the
[official reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/index.html) for arguments.
Newer releases may add functions. There is no need to install an extension
package just to complete the core examples.
